label: Checkout timeout alert
description: Latency budget breach on the checkout path, mixed 502/503 responses.

evidence.title: payment-api: checkout timeout budget breached, mixed 502/503
evidence.detail: Checkout p95 rose from 210ms to 3.9s. Responses are a mix of 502 and 503; 'cache acquisition timed out' dominates the log stream. Monitor: checkout.latency_budget_breach{service=payment-api}.

evidence.title: payment-api v2.18.1 deployed 6 minutes before the alert
evidence.detail: Settlement metadata prefetch on the checkout path, client pool raised to 150. Deployed by @s.almeida, 14 files changed, flagged medium risk.

evidence.title: payment-api degraded; redis-cache healthy; psp-acquirer-eu degraded
evidence.detail: payment-api status=degraded. redis-cache healthy (1.4ms p95, 150 connected clients). psp-acquirer-eu status=degraded, 480ms p95, error rate 0.4% - inside its SLO.

hint: Latency first, error rate second. The PSP is degraded - check whether that explains anything before assuming it does.

label: Client pool saturation
description: Client pool is full (acquired=150/150) and connections are not being released on the settlement path.

evidence.title: Client pool saturated: acquired 150/150, queued 58, wait p95 690ms
evidence.detail: payment-api client pool is fully acquired with 58 waiters. Wait time is rising monotonically for four minutes with no sign of self-recovery.

evidence.title: Connection not released back to pool (settlement path), open_connections=1402
evidence.detail: connection not released back to pool (settlement path) open_connections=1402, prefetch path leak signature present

evidence.title: Redis healthy: cpu 22%, connected_clients 150, used_memory 508MB
evidence.detail: redis-cache-1 reports healthy: cpu 22%, used_memory 508MB, connected_clients 150. Server-side headroom exists; the client's pool budget is fully consumed.

hint: The client's budget is the constraint. A degraded PSP is a real but separate signal.

label: Restart mitigation applied
description: Reachable only by executing the restart action. Familiar 40 second dip.

evidence.title: After rolling restart: failures 5% for 40s, then pool saturated again
evidence.detail: Workers restarted onto the same v2.18.1 build. Pool recovered to 74/150 for about 40 seconds, then refilled as prefetched clients leaked again.

hint: Same script as before. Compare the elapsed time to the previous incident.

label: Regression after mitigation
description: Failure rate back to 24% with the pool saturated on the same build.

evidence.title: Incident returned to 24% failures 32s after the restart
evidence.detail: cache acquisition timed out again, pool acquired 150/150, v2.18.1 still deployed. The mitigation is confirmed temporary.

hint: A second mitigation will behave identically. Change something structural: rollback or pool configuration.

label: Service recovered
description: Rollback plus pool configuration, stable at baseline.

evidence.title: Resolved: pool 71/200, no 502/503, checkout 99.1%
evidence.detail: payment-api rolled back to v2.18.0 with client pool 200. Failures cleared, pool wait 2ms, checkout success 99.1%.

hint: Second resolution of the same pattern. Generate the postmortem and promote the pattern to a service-level memory.
